lab.title: Read the network from the inside out
lab.scenario: A web service is unreachable from another host. Gather evidence layer by layer before changing anything.

steps.text: Record interfaces, addresses, and default route.
steps.verify: Identify the interface with the default gateway.

steps.text: Inspect NetworkManager device and connection state.
steps.cmd: nmcli device status && nmcli -f NAME,DEVICE,STATE connection show
steps.verify: nmcli should show ens3 connected and the active connection name.

steps.text: Check whether a web server is listening and on which address.
steps.verify: ss -tlnp should show a LISTEN socket on port 80 or 443 if a web server is running.

steps.text: Test DNS resolution through the system resolver.
steps.verify: getent hosts localhost should resolve to 127.0.0.1 and ::1.

steps.text: Inspect the firewall zone and list allowed services.
steps.verify: If http is missing, that is a candidate cause — but confirm the listener first.

quiz.q: Which command shows listening TCP sockets with processes?
quiz.why: ss -tlnp filters TCP, listening, numeric, with process information. ip route shows the routing table.

quiz.q: A service is listening only on 127.0.0.1:8080. Can a remote host connect?
options: No, loopback is local to the host
quiz.why: 127.0.0.1 is the loopback address. A remote client cannot reach a socket bound only there.

quiz.q: What happens if you add a firewalld rule without --permanent?
options: It applies at runtime but may disappear on reload or reboot
quiz.why: Runtime changes are temporary. Use --permanent and reload to keep the rule.
